name: queue_message_sync
prose: Sends a message through the single synchronous slot (vchiq_core.c:1007-1110, static, returns VCHIQ_STATUS_T). Unless the message type is VCHIQ_MSG_RESUME it takes state->sync_mutex with lmutex_lock_interruptible and returns VCHIQ_RETRY if that is interrupted; for RESUME it does not take the mutex (the caller is expected to hold it, since the function unlocks it below). It waits for the local sync_release event, reads the sync slot header (logging an error if its msgid is not PADDING) and, if a service is given, copies the elements from user/kernel space into the header data with vchiq_copy_from_user: on a failed copy it unlocks sync_mutex (also for RESUME), increments the service error count and returns VCHIQ_ERROR; on success it updates the service tx statistics. Without a service it memcpy's the single element when size != 0 (with a WARN_ON if count and size are inconsistent). It then sets header->size and msgid, issues a write barrier, signals the remote sync_trigger and unlocks sync_mutex unless the message type is VCHIQ_MSG_PAUSE (for PAUSE the mutex stays locked after a successful return, for RESUME the unlock releases a mutex that this function did not take). It returns VCHIQ_SUCCESS.
note: Slice cut the head (real function at vchiq_core.c:1007). Reviewer round 15 right (the RESUME path skips the lock but still unlocks; the caller must hold sync_mutex, 1016-1018 and 1106-1107). Callees not read.

name: x86emuOp32_opcFF_word_RM
prose: Static void (x86emu.c:4085-4120) emulating the 32-bit opcode 0xFF group: INC (reg field 0), DEC (1) and PUSH (6) on a 32-bit r/m operand. It does not decode the modrm byte itself (the dispatcher must already have set emu->cur_mod and cur_rh, since this function never calls fetch_decode_modrm). For a memory operand (cur_mod != 3) it computes the address with decode_rl_address and ALWAYS fetches the 32-bit value from memory (fetch_data_long), whatever the reg field is; then for reg 0 it increments the value with inc_long and stores it back, for reg 1 it decrements with dec_long and stores it back, for reg 6 it pushes the value with push_long, and for any other reg value it does nothing further (the memory read still happened). For a register operand (cur_mod == 3) it gets the 32-bit register pointer and does the same three operations in place (inc, dec, push) and nothing for other reg values. Flags are updated by inc_long/dec_long (not read).
note: Reviewers: original right (modrm must already be decoded, no fetch_decode_modrm call); round 15 right (for other reg values with a memory operand the fetch at line 4092 still occurs).

name: rcl_byte
prose: Static function (x86emu.c:6703-6767) returning the 8-bit result of rotate-left-through-carry of d by s positions (the slice is the preceding part). It starts with res = d and cnt = s % 9. If cnt is 0 it returns d unchanged and touches no flag. Otherwise it takes the new carry cf as bit (8 - cnt) of d, builds res = (d << cnt) & 0xff, ORs in (d >> (9 - cnt)) masked to cnt-1 bits, and, if the CF flag is currently set, sets bit (cnt - 1) of res. It then sets CF to cf and sets OF only when cnt == 1 (OF = XOR of the new CF and the new top bit; for cnt != 1 OF is cleared by CONDITIONAL_SET_FLAG with a false condition, i.e. it is explicitly written, not left unchanged). SF, ZF, PF and AF are not modified. It returns (uint8_t) res.
note: Reviewer round 1 right (SF/ZF/PF/AF are not updated, only CF and OF); contract dropped (names not in file). Macro CONDITIONAL_SET_FLAG semantics (that a false condition clears the flag) assumed from its name, not read.

name: rol_byte
prose: Static function (x86emu.c:6969-7007) returning the 8-bit result of rotating d left by s positions (s is a count that can be 0 to 8 or larger). It starts with res = d; if cnt = s % 8 is non-zero it computes res = (d << cnt) | ((d >> (8 - cnt)) & ((1 << cnt) - 1)) and sets OF with CONDITIONAL_SET_FLAG(s == 1 && XOR2(...)), i.e. the OF flag is written (cleared unless s == 1 and the XOR condition holds) in that branch only. Then, if s != 0 (not s % 8 != 0) it sets CF from the low bit of res. So for s == 8 (cnt == 0) the value is returned unchanged and OF is left untouched, but CF is still set from bit 0 of d; for s == 0 no flag is modified. Other flags are not touched. It returns (uint8_t) res.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the OF update is inside the s % 8 != 0 branch, so s = 8 leaves OF unchanged while CF is still updated because that test is s != 0 (x86emu.c:6987-7005).

name: xz_dec_bcj_run
prose: Runs the BCJ filter on top of the LZMA2 decoder (xz_dec_bcj.c:417-525, returns enum xz_ret). First, if filtered bytes are pending in the temp buffer it flushes them with bcj_flush; if some remain it returns XZ_OK, and if none remain and the stored result is XZ_STREAM_END it returns XZ_STREAM_END. Then, if the temp buffer fits in the free output space (or is empty), it copies the temp bytes to the output and advances out_pos (without changing s->temp.size at that moment), runs xz_dec_lzma2_run into the output, and returns the lzma2 result immediately if it is neither XZ_STREAM_END nor XZ_OK, or is XZ_OK in single_call mode; in that early return s->temp.size still holds its old value even though those bytes were already copied out. Otherwise it applies bcj_apply to the new output, returns XZ_STREAM_END at the end of stream, saves the unfiltered tail of the output into the temp buffer (sets s->temp.size, moves out_pos back and copies the tail) and returns XZ_OK if the output buffer has room left after that. If output space remains afterwards it decodes into the temp buffer with the output pointers swapped, restores them, returns any error code (not XZ_OK/XZ_STREAM_END), applies bcj_apply to the temp buffer, marks everything filtered at stream end, flushes, and returns XZ_OK if filtered bytes remain. Finally it returns s->ret (XZ_OK or XZ_STREAM_END).
note: Reviewers: original right (the empty annotation omitted the return paths); round 15 right (on the early return after copying temp to out, s->temp.size is not updated, xz_dec_bcj.c:449-458 vs 469). Callees not read.

name: xz_dec_microlzma_run
prose: Runs the MicroLZMA decoder (xz_dec_lzma2.c:1215-1291, returns enum xz_ret). If the sequence is not yet SEQ_LZMA_RUN: in SEQ_PROPERTIES it returns XZ_OK when no input is available, returns XZ_DATA_ERROR if lzma_props rejects the (inverted) properties byte, and moves to SEQ_LZMA_PREPARE; then it returns XZ_DATA_ERROR if the compressed size is below RC_INIT_BYTES or above 3U << 30, returns XZ_OK if rc_read_init needs more input, subtracts RC_INIT_BYTES, switches to SEQ_LZMA_RUN and resets the dictionary. In single-call mode it limits dict.end to the free output space. It then loops: it sets the dictionary limit to the smaller of the free output space and the remaining uncompressed size, runs lzma2_lzma (a false result returns XZ_DATA_ERROR), flushes the dictionary and subtracts the flushed bytes from the uncompressed count. When the uncompressed count reaches 0 it returns XZ_STREAM_END, but only when pedantic_microlzma is set does it first require compressed == 0, lzma.len == 0 and a finished range coder (otherwise XZ_DATA_ERROR); without pedantic mode those checks are not made. Otherwise it returns XZ_OK if the output buffer is full or if the input is exhausted while the compressed bytes still needed exceed the temp buffer, else loops again.
note: Reviewers: original right (XZ_STREAM_END is returned when the uncompressed size is reached, 1274-1281); round 15 WRONG: the pedantic checks are conditional on s->lzma2.pedantic_microlzma (1275-1279). Callees not read.

name: deflate_rle
prose: Compression strategy for Z_RLE (deflate.c:2086-2151, local block_state). It loops: when lookahead is at most MAX_MATCH it calls fill_window (which may modify s->insert and other window state); after that, if lookahead is still at most MAX_MATCH and flush == Z_NO_FLUSH it returns need_more (so need_more is returned only for Z_NO_FLUSH with insufficient lookahead); if lookahead is 0 it leaves the loop to flush. It sets match_length to 0 and, if lookahead >= MIN_MATCH and strstart > 0, scans the window for a run of the byte before strstart (up to MAX_MATCH, capped at lookahead). A run of at least MIN_MATCH is emitted as a distance-1 match (_tr_tally_dist, advancing strstart and reducing lookahead), otherwise one literal is emitted. When the tally says the block is full it does FLUSH_BLOCK(s, 0), a macro that can itself return need_more or finish_started when the output buffer is full. After the loop it sets s->insert = 0; for Z_FINISH it flushes the final block (FLUSH_BLOCK(s, 1), again possibly returning finish_started) and returns finish_done; otherwise, if there are pending symbols it flushes a block (FLUSH_BLOCK(s, 0)) and returns block_done.
note: Reviewers: original right (need_more needs Z_NO_FLUSH and lookahead <= MAX_MATCH, 2098-2099); round 15 right (the need_more path goes through fill_window, which can change s->insert, and the early return does not reset s->insert). FLUSH_BLOCK and fill_window not read.

name: fill_window
prose: Local void (deflate.c:252-376) that refills the deflate sliding window from the input. It asserts lookahead < MIN_LOOKAHEAD, then loops (do/while). Each iteration computes the free space 'more' at the end of the window. When strstart has reached at least wsize + MAX_DIST it slides the window: the upper half (wsize - more bytes) is copied down by wsize, match_start, strstart and block_start are reduced by wsize, s->insert is lowered to strstart if it was larger, the hash tables are slid (slide_hash), and more grows by wsize. If strm->avail_in is 0 it leaves the loop; otherwise it reads up to 'more' bytes with read_buf into the window after the lookahead and adds the count to lookahead. If lookahead + insert is at least MIN_MATCH it initialises ins_h from the bytes at strstart - insert and inserts pending hash entries (decrementing s->insert for each one until lookahead + insert falls below MIN_MATCH). The loop repeats while lookahead < MIN_LOOKAHEAD and input remains. After the loop, if high_water < window_size it zeroes memory beyond the data to avoid uninitialised reads: when high_water is below the current data end (curr = strstart + lookahead) it zeroes up to WIN_INIT bytes starting at curr (not at high_water) and sets high_water = curr + that count; otherwise, when high_water is below curr + WIN_INIT, it zeroes from high_water for the missing bytes (bounded by the window size) and advances high_water. It asserts strstart <= window_size - MIN_LOOKAHEAD at the end. Returns void.
note: Reviewers: round 15 right (when high_water < curr the zeroing starts at curr, deflate.c:351-359). The macros UPDATE_HASH and the helpers slide_hash/read_buf were not read.

name: deflate
prose: Public int ZEXPORT deflate(z_streamp strm, int flush) (deflate.c:981-1290). It returns Z_STREAM_ERROR without setting strm->msg if the stream/state check fails or flush is outside 0..Z_BLOCK. With ERR_RETURN (which sets strm->msg to the error text before returning) it returns Z_STREAM_ERROR for next_out NULL, avail_in != 0 with next_in NULL, or a finished stream called with a flush other than Z_FINISH, and Z_BUF_ERROR if avail_out == 0. It records old_flush, stores the new flush in s->last_flush, and if pending output exists it calls flush_pending: if avail_out is then 0 it sets s->last_flush = -1 (not flush) and returns Z_OK; else if there is no input and the flush level does not exceed the previous one (and is not Z_FINISH) it returns Z_BUF_ERROR; a finished stream with more input also returns Z_BUF_ERROR. It writes the zlib or gzip header (states INIT, GZIP, EXTRA, NAME, COMMENT, HCRC), returning Z_OK with last_flush = -1 whenever flushing the header leaves pending bytes. Then, if there is input, lookahead, or a non-NO_FLUSH request on an unfinished stream, it runs the strategy function (deflate_stored, deflate_huff, deflate_rle or the table function for the level): finish_started/finish_done set the FINISH state; need_more or finish_started return Z_OK (with last_flush = -1 if avail_out is 0); block_done emits the alignment or empty stored block for PARTIAL, SYNC or FULL flush (clearing the hash for Z_FULL_FLUSH), flushes pending and returns Z_OK with last_flush = -1 when avail_out is 0. If flush is not Z_FINISH it returns Z_OK; if the stream has no wrapper (wrap <= 0) it returns Z_STREAM_END; otherwise it writes the gzip or zlib trailer, flushes, makes wrap negative so the trailer is written once, and returns Z_OK if output is still pending, else Z_STREAM_END.
note: Reviewers: round 2 right (the Z_OK return after a pending flush with avail_out == 0 sets last_flush = -1, not flush, deflate.c:1004-1007); round 15 right that strm->msg is set only by the ERR_RETURN paths, not by the initial Z_STREAM_ERROR. Partly read: the gzip header states (lines 1067-1190) were skimmed. Deflate strategy functions and flush_pending not read.

name: inflate
prose: Public int ZEXPORT inflate(z_streamp strm, int flush) (inflate.c:474-1153); this slice covers the early part of it (header, dictionary, stored blocks, dynamic table setup) before the decoding loop. It returns Z_STREAM_ERROR immediately, with no counters updated, if the state check fails, next_out is NULL or next_in is NULL with avail_in != 0. Otherwise it loads the stream into local variables and runs a state machine on state->mode. Header states (HEAD, FLAGS, TIME, OS, EXLEN, EXTRA, NAME, COMMENT, HCRC, DICTID) read the zlib or gzip header; invalid headers, bad window sizes, header checks or flags set the mode to BAD with a message (reported as Z_DATA_ERROR). In the DICT state without a preset dictionary it restores the stream pointers and returns Z_NEED_DICT directly (no counter or check updates). Block states (TYPE, STORED, COPY, TABLE, LENLENS, CODELENS) handle block headers, stored blocks and Huffman table construction, and set BAD on invalid data. Input or output exhaustion (no input, or no output space) and the Z_BLOCK / Z_TREES flush modes jump to inf_leave. The mode MEM returns Z_MEM_ERROR directly and SYNC or an unknown mode returns Z_STREAM_ERROR directly. Normal exits go through inf_leave, which stores the pointers back, updates the window (a failure of updatewindow sets mode MEM and returns Z_MEM_ERROR), updates total_in, total_out, the running check and strm->adler, sets data_type, and turns Z_OK into Z_BUF_ERROR when no progress was made (in == 0 and out == 0) or flush == Z_FINISH. So the return values are Z_OK, Z_STREAM_END, Z_NEED_DICT, Z_DATA_ERROR, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_BUF_ERROR or Z_STREAM_ERROR. After Z_DATA_ERROR (BAD) or Z_MEM_ERROR (MEM) the stream is in a terminal state and cannot be resumed.
note: Slice shows the head of the function. Reviewers: original right (Z_NEED_DICT and Z_MEM_ERROR are possible returns); round 15 right (Z_DATA_ERROR and Z_MEM_ERROR leave a terminal BAD/MEM mode, inflate.c:1119-1124 and 1130-1133). Partly read: the per-state decoding bodies were only scanned for their return, break and jump points.

name: inflate
prose: Public int ZEXPORT inflate(z_streamp strm, int flush) (inflate.c:474-1153); this slice covers the middle part: block-table reading and the decoding of codes and copying of matches. Within it a code table or length error sets the mode to BAD (message set, later returned as Z_DATA_ERROR); running out of input or output goes to inf_leave; Z_BLOCK and Z_TREES flush values stop at block boundaries (inf_leave) when requested. Whatever the path, the exits of the whole function are: Z_STREAM_ERROR before any counter update (invalid stream, or the default/SYNC mode), Z_NEED_DICT returned from the DICT state after restoring pointers but before totals and checks are updated, Z_MEM_ERROR returned directly in mode MEM or after a failed updatewindow, and otherwise the normal inf_leave path which updates total_in, total_out, state->total, the check value and adler (only when output was produced and wrap & 4), data_type, and converts a Z_OK without progress (or with flush == Z_FINISH) to Z_BUF_ERROR. Consumed input is not always matched by produced output: header, table and trailer bytes are consumed without producing output.
note: Slice shows a middle part of the same function. Reviewers: original right (success can consume header bytes without producing output); round 15 right (Z_NEED_DICT, Z_MEM_ERROR and the early Z_STREAM_ERROR returns skip the total/adler/data_type updates, inflate.c:489-491, 703-708, 1146). Partly read.

name: inflate

name: HUF_setMaxHeight
prose: Static U32 (huf_compress.c:376-498) that limits the Huffman code length to targetNbBits. The caller must supply huffNode sorted by decreasing count (so nbBits is non-decreasing along the array, the largest length at lastNonNull). It returns largestBits unchanged and does nothing else if the largest code length is already <= targetNbBits. Otherwise it computes totalCost by clamping every code longer than targetNbBits to targetNbBits (walking down from lastNonNull), converts the cost to units of 2^-targetNbBits, then repays that cost by lengthening (nbBits++) symbols that have fewer bits than the target, chosen by the rankLast table (the rank with the cheapest increase in total count); if the repayment overshoots (totalCost < 0) it shortens some symbols again (nbBits-- on the symbols just after the last rank-1 one). When it finishes the Kraft sum (the sum of 2^-nbBits) is again 1 under the assumption that the input satisfied it, and it returns targetNbBits. The function modifies huffNode[*].nbBits in place; it asserts (debug builds only) divisibility and positivity of totalCost and rank validity, and it does not check the sortedness or the Kraft precondition itself.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (the sorted and sum preconditions and the rank-sum postcondition were missing). Partly read: the rankLast bookkeeping (lines 410-493) was read for structure, the cost-repayment arithmetic was not independently verified.

name: ZSTD_buildBlockEntropyStats_sequences
prose: Static size_t (zstd_compress.c:3759-3789) that computes the FSE encoding choices for the sequences of a block. It derives nbSeq from the sequence store and splits the workspace: the first (MaxSeq + 1) unsigned values are counts and the remainder, of size wkspSize - (MaxSeq + 1) * sizeof(unsigned), is the entropy workspace; the caller must therefore pass wkspSize of at least that count area (the size_t subtraction would underflow otherwise; the code does not check it). If nbSeq != 0 it calls ZSTD_buildSequencesStatistics (which fills the FSE tables in nextEntropy and writes table headers into fseMetadata->fseTablesBuffer); if nbSeq == 0 it calls ZSTD_buildDummySequencesStatistics(nextEntropy), which only sets the three repeat modes of nextEntropy to FSE_repeat_none and returns set_basic for all three types with size 0 and does not build any FSE table. A non-zero error in stats.size is returned through FORWARD_IF_ERROR before anything is stored in fseMetadata. On success it stores the three symbol encoding types and lastCountSize in fseMetadata and returns stats.size (the number of header bytes written, 0 in the dummy case).
note: Reviewers: original right (minimum wkspSize precondition, 3774); round 15 right (the nbSeq == 0 path only resets the repeat modes, zstd_compress.c:3746-3750). Callee ZSTD_buildSequencesStatistics not read.

name: ZSTD_compressContinue_internal
prose: Static size_t (zstd_compress.c:4792-4851) that compresses one chunk or block, returning the number of bytes written to dst or an error code. It returns the stage_wrong error if the context stage is ZSTDcs_created (not initialised). If frame is set and the stage is ZSTDcs_init it writes the frame header (error forwarded), advances dst, reduces dstCapacity and sets the stage to ZSTDcs_ongoing; the stage change therefore happens only in that case (not for non-frame calls or after the header was already written). If srcSize == 0 it returns fhSize right away (0 when no header was written), without generating a block and without updating consumedSrcSize or producedCSize. Otherwise it updates the match-state window (and the LDM window when enabled), for non-frame calls runs overflow correction, then compresses with ZSTD_compress_frameChunk (frame) or ZSTD_compressBlock_internal (not frame); an error is forwarded before any counter changes. It then adds srcSize to consumedSrcSize and cSize + fhSize to producedCSize, and, when a source size was pledged, returns the srcSize_wrong error if the consumed size exceeds the pledge. On success it returns cSize + fhSize.
note: Reviewers: original right (the stage and counters are not advanced on the non-frame or zero-length paths); round 15 right (the srcSize == 0 early return skips the counter updates, zstd_compress.c:4815). Callees not read.

name: ZSTD_compressStream_generic
prose: Static size_t (zstd_compress.c:6103-6287), the newer streaming state machine that supports buffered and stable input/output buffers. Before the loop, in stable input mode it rewinds input->pos and ip by the bytes left unconsumed by the previous call (stableIn_notConsumed) and clears that counter; the other preconditions on the buffers are assertions. Loop on streamStage: zcss_init returns the error init_missing immediately (so an uninitialised stream is handled here by an error, not assumed away); zcss_load either compresses the whole remaining input directly with ZSTD_compressEnd_public when flushMode is ZSTD_e_end and the output has room (or the output buffer mode is stable), sets frameEnded and resets the session, or, in buffered input mode, copies input into the internal buffer (stopping for ZSTD_e_continue when the block is not yet full, or for ZSTD_e_flush when nothing new is buffered), or, in stable input mode, stops for ZSTD_e_continue when fewer than blockSizeMax bytes remain (recording them in stableIn_notConsumed and pretending they were consumed) or for ZSTD_e_flush when the input is empty; it then compresses one block (ZSTD_compressEnd_public for the last block, else ZSTD_compressContinue; errors are forwarded), directly into the output when it has room or in stable output mode, else into the internal buffer followed by the zcss_flush stage, which copies buffered output out, stops when the output is full, and after a full flush either ends the frame (reset session) or returns to zcss_load. On the normal exit it stores the input and output positions and returns 0 when frameEnded is set, else ZSTD_nextInputSizeHint(zcs). Error returns happen before the positions are written back.
note: Previously unreviewed by a second reviewer; checked against the code. Original reviewer right (init_missing is an error return, 6142-6143). Partly read: lines 6200-6250 (direct-compress and stable-output branches) were only skimmed.

name: ZSTD_decompressContinue
prose: Public size_t ZSTD_decompressContinue(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize) (zstd_decompress.c:1275-1432), the buffer-less streaming decoder step; it returns the number of bytes written to dst (0 for header or checksum steps) or an error code, not a count of bytes consumed. It first returns the srcSize_wrong error, before touching any state (processedCSize is not yet updated), if srcSize is not exactly the size the context expects next. It then checks continuity of dst, adds srcSize to processedCSize, and switches on dctx->stage: getFrameHeaderSize detects a skippable frame (copies the bytes, sets expected and stage decodeSkippableHeader) or reads the frame header size (a header size error is returned, after processedCSize was already increased), copies the bytes and sets stage decodeFrameHeader; decodeFrameHeader parses the header (errors forwarded) and sets expected to the block header size; decodeBlockHeader reads the block size (error if it exceeds the block size maximum; both errors can leave expected/stage as they were or partly changed); an empty block either ends the frame (to the checksum or a new frame header stage) or advances to the next block header; decompressBlock/LastBlock handles compressed, raw and RLE blocks (an invalid block type, a decode error, or a block larger than the maximum returns an error, in some cases after dctx->expected was changed), adds the produced size to decodedSize, updates the checksum, sets previousDstEnd, and returns the produced size; at the last block it checks the frame content size (corruption_detected on mismatch) and moves to checksum or the next frame; checkChecksum compares the stored 32-bit checksum when validating (checksum_wrong on mismatch) and finishes the frame returning 0; decodeSkippableHeader and skipFrame only advance the stage and return 0; an unknown stage returns the GENERIC error.
note: Reviewers: original right (the return is the decompressed byte count or 0, and an error can occur after expected/stage were already changed, e.g. raw/rle expected updates at 1349 and 1360); round 15 right (processedCSize is not updated on the early srcSize_wrong return, 1279 vs 1282). Callees not read.

name: COVER_buildDictionary
prose: Static size_t (cover.c:727-777) that fills a dictionary buffer from the best segments and returns tail, the offset in dictBuffer where the filled region starts (the dictionary occupies dictBuffer[tail .. capacity)). It starts with tail = dictBufferCapacity, computes the epoch layout with COVER_computeEpochs and a limit maxZeroScoreRun = MAX(10, MIN(100, epochs.num >> 3)). It loops epoch by epoch (cycling) while tail > 0: it selects the best segment of the epoch (COVER_selectSegment); a segment with score 0 increments the zero-score run and ends the loop (break) when that run reaches the limit, else moves to the next epoch; a non-zero score resets the run. It sizes the segment as MIN(segment.end - segment.begin + d - 1, tail) and breaks out of the loop if that size is smaller than parameters.d (this includes the case where the remaining tail is smaller than d, not only the case of a short selected segment). Otherwise it subtracts the size from tail and copies the segment from the samples to dict + tail (the buffer is filled from the back). The loop ends when tail reaches 0, when too many consecutive zero-score epochs occur, or when the size is below d, so the returned tail is 0 only when the dictionary was filled completely; in the other two exits it is greater than 0. It prints progress (display level) and returns tail.
note: Reviewers: original right (zero-score and small-segment breaks leave tail > 0); round 15 right (the break also occurs when the remaining tail is below d, cover.c:762-765).

name: ss_mintrosort
prose: Static void (divsufsort.c:400-531) that sorts the suffix-array range [first, last) by multikey introsort, comparing the characters T[PA[*x] + depth] starting at the given depth and continuing to deeper characters (it does not stop after the first depth characters). It uses an explicit local stack of pending ranges (STACK_PUSH / STACK_POP) instead of recursion, so subranges of equal characters are re-sorted inside the same call at depth + 1; the function returns (through the STACK_POP macro when the stack is empty) only when all pending ranges have been sorted. Small ranges (<= SS_INSERTIONSORT_THRESHOLD) are finished with ss_insertionsort, a range whose depth-limit counter reaches zero is handled with ss_heapsort, and otherwise a pivot is chosen with ss_pivot, the range is three-way partitioned around the pivot character, and the less-than, equal (next depth) and greater-than parts are pushed or processed. Elements of the range of PA indices are permuted in place (the sort moves entries of the range; T and PA are only read). It returns nothing and has no failure result.
note: Previously unreviewed by a second reviewer. Original reviewer right that it recurses (via its own stack) and sorts from depth onward. Partly read: ss_partition, ss_pivot, ss_insertionsort and ss_heapsort bodies and the STACK_* macro definitions were not read.

name: HUF_readStats
prose: Static size_t (zstd_v02.c:1481-1557) reading a Huffman weight table header. It returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) for empty input. The first byte iSize selects the format: >= 242 is an RLE header (oSize from a 14-entry table, all hwSize bytes of huffWeight set to 1, iSize = 0, with no check that oSize is smaller than hwSize); 128..241 is an uncompressed 4-bit header (oSize = iSize - 127; returns srcSize_wrong if the packed bytes do not fit in srcSize and corruption_detected if oSize >= hwSize, then unpacks the nibbles); below 128 the weights are FSE-compressed: srcSize_wrong if iSize + 1 > srcSize, otherwise FSE_decompress into at most hwSize - 1 weights (an FSE error is returned as is). It then zeroes rankStats, counts the weights and sums weightTotal = sum of (1 << w) >> 1, returning corruption_detected if any weight is >= HUF_ABSOLUTEMAX_TABLELOG, if weightTotal is 0, or if the derived tableLog (highbit(weightTotal) + 1) exceeds HUF_ABSOLUTEMAX_TABLELOG. It then derives the implied last weight from rest = 2^tableLog - weightTotal: corruption_detected unless rest itself is a power of two (it is the remaining total rest, not weightTotal, that must be a power of two); the last weight is stored at huffWeight[oSize] and counted. Finally corruption_detected unless rankStats[1] is at least 2 and even. On success it sets *nbSymbolsPtr = oSize + 1 and *tableLogPtr = tableLog and returns iSize + 1, the number of header bytes consumed.
note: Previously unreviewed except round 1: round 1 right (the code checks that the remaining total 'rest' is a power of two, not that weightTotal is, 1543-1545). Callees (FSE_decompress, BIT_highbit32) not read.

name: HUF_decompress4X2
prose: Static size_t (zstd_v02.c:1752-1763) wrapper that decodes a 4-stream single-symbol Huffman block. It builds a decoding table on the stack with HUF_readDTableX2 from the start of cSrc and returns that call's error if it fails; the non-error result is the number of header bytes consumed. If the header consumed cSrcSize bytes or more it returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) (so this error can be returned before the size check inside the callee). Otherwise it skips the header and returns HUF_decompress4X2_usingDTable(dst, dstSize, ip, cSrcSize - header, DTable). That callee (zstd_v02.c:1656-1750) returns corruption_detected if the remaining input is smaller than 10 bytes (a jump table plus one byte per stream), returns any error of the four BIT_initDStream calls, returns corruption_detected on overflow of the fourth stream length, on stream pointers crossing their segments, or when the bit streams are not fully consumed at the end, and otherwise returns dstSize (all dstSize bytes decoded).
note: Previously only reviewed by earlier rounds: original right (corruption_detected can come from the callee for malformed payloads, 1732-1745); round 2 right (srcSize_wrong can be returned first when the header consumes everything, 1759). Callee bodies HUF_readDTableX2 and the decode macros not read.

name: HUF_decompress4X6_usingDTable
prose: Static size_t (zstd_v02.c:2373-2468) decoding a 4-stream quad-symbol Huffman block with a prepared table. It returns ERROR(corruption_detected) if cSrcSize < 10 (jump table plus one byte per stream). It reads the three 16-bit stream lengths from the jump table, derives the fourth length as cSrcSize - (length1 + length2 + length3 + 6) and returns corruption_detected if that wrapped around. It initialises the four bit streams with BIT_initDStream and returns that call's error code as is (not forced to corruption_detected; for example srcSize_wrong is possible). Four streams are decoded in an interleaved loop while all streams are unfinished and the output position is far enough from the end; then it returns corruption_detected if any of the first three output pointers passed the start of the next segment, finishes the tails with the per-stream decoders and returns corruption_detected unless all four streams ended exactly at their end; otherwise it returns dstSize.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (a BIT_initDStream failure returns that call's own error code, 2417-2424). Callees not read.

name: BIT_reloadDStream
prose: MEM_STATIC BIT_DStream_status (zstd_v03.c:404-434) that refills the bit container of a backward bit stream and reports its status. If bitsConsumed exceeds the container width in bits it returns BIT_DStream_overflow immediately, without refilling. If ptr is at least one container width above start, it moves ptr back by the whole consumed bytes, keeps the remaining bit count (bitsConsumed &= 7), reloads the container from memory and returns BIT_DStream_unfinished. Otherwise, if ptr == start it returns BIT_DStream_endOfBuffer when fewer than a full container of bits was consumed, else BIT_DStream_completed, again without refilling. In the remaining case (ptr strictly between start and start + container size) it computes nbBytes = bitsConsumed >> 3; if ptr - nbBytes would go below start it limits nbBytes to ptr - start and the result becomes BIT_DStream_endOfBuffer; when ptr - nbBytes equals start exactly the result stays BIT_DStream_unfinished. It then moves ptr back by nbBytes, reduces bitsConsumed by nbBytes * 8, reloads the container and returns the result. So the container is refilled only in the unfinished/short-buffer paths, not in the overflow, completed, or ptr == start returns.
note: Reviewers: original right (no refill on overflow, completed or ptr == start); round 15 right (the endOfBuffer test is a strict '<', so ptr - nbBytes == start returns unfinished, 424-428).

name: ZBUFFv05_decompressContinue
prose: Buffered streaming decompression step (zstd_v05.c:3842-3994, returns size_t: a size hint or an error). In/out parameters *srcSizePtr and *maxDstSizePtr are the available input and output on entry and the consumed and produced bytes on a normal exit (written at 3986-3987); they are NOT updated on the early returns. It loops over zbc->stage: ZBUFFv05ds_init returns ERROR(init_missing); readHeader calls ZSTDv05_getFrameParams on the input (error returned), and if the header is not complete it copies the input bytes into headerBuffer, sets stage loadHeader and returns headerSize - hPos without writing any output and without updating *srcSizePtr; loadHeader appends more input to the header buffer and, if the header is still incomplete, returns the remaining count with the stage unchanged (loadHeader) and *srcSizePtr not updated; once the header is complete decodeHeader allocates the input and output buffers (ERROR(memory_allocation) on failure), copies any buffered header bytes into the input buffer and goes to load, else to read; read gets the next needed input size (0 means end of frame: stage back to init and exit the loop), decodes directly from the caller's input when enough is available (error returned), or switches to load; load fills the input buffer (corruption_detected if the request does not fit), exits the loop to wait for more input when it has too little, and decodes (a zero decoded size means a header only); flush copies decoded bytes to the output and either returns to read or exits the loop when the output is full; an unknown stage returns ERROR(GENERIC). On loop exit it stores the consumed and produced sizes and returns the next input size hint (including the block header size, minus the bytes already loaded).
note: Reviewers: original right (the header-incomplete path writes no output and does not update *srcSizePtr, 3862-3866); round 15 right (an incomplete loadHeader leaves the stage unchanged, 3876-3878). Note: the filtered view I used hid the '*srcSizePtr = ...' assignment at first; it was checked in the raw source (3986-3987). Callees not read.

name: HUFv06_readStats
prose: MEM_STATIC size_t (zstd_v06.c:1798-1865) with the same structure as the v02 HUF_readStats: it returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) for empty input; reads iSize from the first byte; for iSize >= 242 it uses an RLE header (oSize from a 14-entry table, all hwSize bytes of huffWeight set to 1, iSize = 0, no check of oSize against hwSize); for 128..241 an uncompressed 4-bit header (srcSize_wrong if the packed bytes do not fit, corruption_detected if oSize >= hwSize); below 128 an FSE-compressed header (srcSize_wrong if iSize + 1 > srcSize, otherwise FSEv06_decompress into at most hwSize - 1 weights, an FSE error being returned). It zeroes rankStats, accumulates the counts and weightTotal, returning corruption_detected for a weight >= HUFv06_ABSOLUTEMAX_TABLELOG, for weightTotal == 0 and for tableLog above the maximum. It writes *tableLogPtr = tableLog at that point, before the remaining checks, so the output is written even when a later check fails. It then requires the remaining total rest = 2^tableLog - weightTotal to be a power of two (corruption_detected otherwise, it is rest and not weightTotal that is tested), stores the implied last weight at huffWeight[oSize] and counts it, and returns corruption_detected unless rankStats[1] is at least 2 and even. On success it sets *nbSymbolsPtr = oSize + 1 and returns iSize + 1 (the header bytes consumed).
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (it is the remaining weight total, rest, that must be a power of two, 1852-1854). Callees not read.

name: ZSTDv07_decodeSeqHeaders
prose: Static size_t (zstd_v07.c:3393-3441) that decodes the sequences section header: the sequence count and the three FSE table descriptions. It returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) if srcSize < MIN_SEQUENCES_SIZE. It reads the first byte as the sequence count: 0 stores *nbSeqPtr = 0 and returns 1 at once; 1..127 is the count itself; 128..254 uses a second byte, and 255 uses a 16-bit value plus LONGNBSEQ (srcSize_wrong if those extra bytes are missing). *nbSeqPtr is written before the later checks, so it is set even if an error follows. It then requires four more bytes (srcSize_wrong otherwise), reads the three 2-bit table types, and builds the literal-length, offset and match-length decoding tables with ZSTDv07_buildSeqTable; any error from a table build is converted to ERROR(corruption_detected) (the original error is not returned). On success it returns the number of header bytes consumed (ip - istart), which is 1 for a zero count and at least 2 otherwise (count byte plus the type byte when all three tables are RAW/RLE-free, i.e. no table bytes), not at least 4.
note: Previously unreviewed by a second reviewer except round 1: round 1 right (the return can be 2 when no table bytes are present, 3405-3440). The 'ip + 4 > iend' check at 3420 requires 4 bytes of input after the count, but the returned consumed size can be smaller. Callee not read.

name: ZSTDv07_execSequence
prose: size_t (zstd_v07.c:3534-3609) that executes one decoded sequence (copies litLength literals, then matchLength bytes of match) at op, returning the sequence length litLength + matchLength on success or an error code. Checks before any copy: ERROR(dstSize_tooSmall) if the literal length plus WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH does not fit in the remaining output, or if litLength + matchLength does not fit; ERROR(corruption_detected) if litLength exceeds the remaining literal buffer (litLimit - *litPtr). It then wild-copies the literals, advances op and *litPtr (so on a later error *litPtr has already been advanced and the literals already written). If the match offset reaches before the current prefix (offset > oLitEnd - base) it returns corruption_detected unless the match lies in the dictionary segment (offset <= oLitEnd - vBase); a match entirely inside the dictionary is copied with memmove and returned; a match crossing from the dictionary into the prefix copies the first part, then continues with the rest (byte by byte near the end of the buffer or when the remainder is shorter than MINMATCH). For a normal in-prefix match it copies the first 8 bytes using the dec32/dec64 tables for offsets below 8 (overlapping copy), then either copies the rest byte by byte up to oMatchEnd when close to the buffer end (using wildcopy while it is still safe), or uses ZSTDv07_wildcopy for the remainder. In all success paths it returns the sequence length (litLength + matchLength) and leaves op conceptually at oMatchEnd (op is a local copy; the caller advances its own pointer by the returned length).
note: Reviewers: round 1 says exactly litLength + matchLength is the return value, which matches 3565, 3575, 3608; the 'no write past the end' claims depend on the wildcopy margin checks at 3548-3549 and 3598. Partly read: ZSTDv07_wildcopy and the copy4/copy8 helpers were not read.

name: ZSTDv07_decompressContinue
prose: Public size_t ZSTDv07_decompressContinue(ZSTDv07_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize) (zstd_v07.c:3933-4029), the buffer-less streaming step; it returns the number of bytes written to dst (0 for header steps) or an error code. It returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) at once, with no state change, if srcSize differs from dctx->expected; if dstCapacity is non-zero it checks continuity. By stage: getFrameHeaderSize (srcSize_wrong if not the minimal header size) detects a skippable-frame magic (copy, stage decodeSkippableHeader) or computes the full header size (error returned), and goes to decodeFrameHeader unless the minimal header is already complete (then it falls through with expected 0); decodeFrameHeader copies the rest of the header, decodes it (error returned) and sets expected to the block header size; decodeBlockHeader reads the block size (error returned); for an end block it checks the 22-bit checksum if the frame has one (checksum_wrong on mismatch), sets expected = 0 and stage getFrameHeaderSize; otherwise it records the block type and size and moves to decompressBlock; decompressBlock handles compressed and raw blocks; an RLE block or an unknown type returns ERROR(GENERIC) BEFORE the stage and expected are reset, so those two paths leave the stage as decompressBlock; for the compressed and raw paths the stage is set back to decodeBlockHeader and expected to the block header size BEFORE the error check of rSize, so a decode error returns an error with the stage and expected already reset (they are not left unchanged). On success it updates previousDstEnd, the checksum and returns rSize. The skippable stages only advance the stage and return 0; an unknown stage returns ERROR(GENERIC).
note: Reviewers: original right (stage and expected are updated before the decodeBlock error return, 4008-4010); round 15 right (the bt_rle and default paths return GENERIC before stage/expected are reset, 3999-4006). Callees not read.

name: BMK_benchMemAdvancedNoAlloc
prose: Static BMK_benchOutcome_t (benchzstd.c:410-777; the packet name BMK_benchMemAdvanced_Internal does not exist and the slice is the middle and tail of this function, ending where BMK_benchMemAdvanced starts at 779). It benchmarks compression and decompression of a set of blocks with caller-provided buffers and returns a BMK_benchOutcome_t that is either an error outcome or a valid result. In decode-only mode it first sums the decompressed size of every file (frame content sizes): an unknown or erroneous content size, a size_t overflow, or a failed allocation of the result buffer returns an error outcome through RETURN_ERROR (the result buffer is freed and replaced first). It then splits the source into blocks, prepares the per-block sizes, and, when multi-threaded measurements are unsupported but several workers were requested, adjusts the worker count. It repeats compression and decompression runs until both are completed, keeping the best speeds: a failed run returns an error outcome ('compression error' / 'decompression error'). After the runs, in compress-and-decompress mode it compares a checksum of the decompressed data with the original and, on mismatch, searches for the first differing byte and prints diagnostic context (this path is reported but is not turned into an error outcome in the part of the code that I read). It prints the result line depending on the display level and returns BMK_benchOutcome_setValidResult(benchResult).
note: Slice cut the head. Partly read: lines 410-540 (setup) were not in the slice, and the middle of the run loop (lines 570-700) and the mismatch-report code were only scanned for returns and control flow, not read line by line.

name: z_inflateReset
prose: Wrapper for inflateReset (zstd_zlibwrapper.c:663-674, ZEXTERN int ZEXPORT z_inflateReset). It logs, and if the wrapper is forced to use zlib (g_ZWRAPdecompressionType == ZWRAP_FORCE_ZLIB) or the stream is not a zstd-wrapped stream (!strm->reserved) it simply returns zlib's inflateReset(strm) (so it does fall back to the zlib reset in those cases). Otherwise it calls ZWRAP_inflateReset_keepDict(strm) and returns its error code if that is not Z_OK; in the zstd branch that helper (lines 641-658) returns Z_STREAM_ERROR if the state pointer is NULL, otherwise re-initialises the ZWRAP decompression context, sets its state to ZWRAP_useReset, zeroes totalInBytes, total_in and total_out and returns Z_OK; it does not call inflateReset itself in this branch, so inflateReset's error cannot be returned from the zstd branch. After the helper succeeds it fetches the state again (returning Z_STREAM_ERROR if NULL, though the helper already checked) and sets decompState to ZWRAP_useInit, then returns Z_OK.
note: Reviewers: original right (fallback to inflateReset when forced to zlib or unreserved, 668-669); round 15 right (the keepDict helper's zstd branch cannot return inflateReset's error, 641-658).

name: db_command
prose: Static void (db_command.c:378-526) that parses and runs one ddb command line. The first token decides: tEOL repeats *last_cmdp with address db_next, no address and count 1; tEXCL runs db_fncall and returns; any non-identifier token prints 'Unrecognized input' and flushes the line. For an identifier it searches cmd_table (then sub-tables via cmd->more): no match prints 'No such command', an ambiguous name prints 'Ambiguous', and help prints the help text; each of these flushes the lexer and returns without executing; if a table has subcommands and the next token is not an identifier it prints a hint and returns. The loop is skipped when cmd_table is NULL, in which case cmd stays NULL and the code after the loop dereferences cmd->flag (a NULL cmd_table with an identifier token would crash), so a non-NULL cmd_table is needed. For commands without CS_OWN it parses '[/modifier] [addr] [,count]': a bad modifier returns; when an address expression parses, db_dot and db_last_addr are set to it immediately (so a later parse failure such as 'Count missing', which flushes and returns, leaves db_dot and db_last_addr already modified); count defaults to -1; unless CS_MORE it skips to end of line. After parsing it sets *last_cmdp = cmd (only on this path; the early returns above do not update it), optionally lets MAC veto the command (prints a message and returns), enables or disables the pager according to dopager, calls (*cmd->fcn)(addr, have_addr, count, modif) when cmd is non-NULL, and finally sets db_dot from db_prev or db_next for CS_SET_DOT commands, else db_next = db_dot.
note: Reviewers: original right (the count-missing error returns after db_dot and db_last_addr were already modified, 520-ish: db_dot at the address-parse step); round 15 right (a NULL cmd_table makes cmd NULL and cmd->flag is read, db_command.c:446-ish).

name: db_check_interrupt
prose: Void function (db_input.c:419-458) that polls the console for pending input during ddb output. It loops: if ddb_prioritize_control_input is false and the raw input buffer has no space (db_raw_space() false) it returns immediately without reading; otherwise it reads one character with cncheckc(): -1 (no character) returns; Ctrl-C calls db_do_interrupt('^C'); Ctrl-S enters a wait loop that keeps calling cncheckc() until it returns Ctrl-Q (a Ctrl-C in that loop also calls db_do_interrupt; a return value of -1 does not leave the loop, it just polls again, so this loop can only be left by Ctrl-Q or by db_do_interrupt); any other character is pushed into the raw buffer with db_raw_push if there is space, else it is dropped and a one-time '--Exceeded input buffer--' message is printed (db_raw_warned). So when the raw buffer is full the pending characters are not all buffered: control characters are processed (if prioritising) and other characters are discarded.
note: Reviewers: original right (full buffer: returns before reading or drops non-control characters); round 15 right (cncheckc() == -1 inside the ^S wait loop does not return, 441-445).

name: db_stop_at_pc
prose: bool function (db_run.c:71-189) deciding whether the debugger should stop at a trap. It first sets *is_breakpoint and *is_watchpoint from the trap type/code (IS_BREAKPOINT_TRAP / IS_WATCHPOINT_TRAP), reads pc, clears single-step, breakpoints and watchpoints, and (where defined) fixes the pc after a breakpoint trap. It looks up a debugger breakpoint at pc: if one exists, it decrements its count; when the count reaches 0 it resets the count to init_count, sets *is_breakpoint = true and returns true; otherwise it returns false (the countdown continues) with *is_breakpoint left at its initial trap classification value (it is not cleared on this path). If no breakpoint is registered at pc and the trap looked like a breakpoint, BKPT_SKIP is applied when defined. In every other path *is_breakpoint is then set to false ('might be a breakpoint, but not ours'). Then, where IS_SSTEP_TRAP is defined: STEP_CONTINUE with a single-step trap returns false, and a non-continue run mode without a single-step trap prints 'Stepping aborted' and returns true. By run mode: STEP_INVISIBLE sets STEP_CONTINUE and returns false; STEP_COUNT returns false; STEP_ONCE returns false (optionally printing the location) while db_loop_count stays above zero after decrement; STEP_RETURN returns false until a return or trap-return instruction (tracking call depth); STEP_CALLT returns false unless the instruction at pc is a call, return or trap return. Otherwise it returns true. It has side effects on the debugger run-mode, loop count, call depth and the breakpoint list.
note: Reviewers: original right (is_breakpoint is cleared for a breakpoint that is not ours, 112); round 2 right (when the countdown is not finished *is_breakpoint keeps its initial trap classification, 105). Macros such as FIXUP_PC_AFTER_BREAK and IS_SSTEP_TRAP are machine dependent and were not expanded.

name: aac_map_command_sg
prose: Static bus_dmamap callback (aac.c:1549-1636; the slice cut the head, and the packet name aac_map_command does not exist) that finishes setting up a command once its data is mapped. The error argument is ignored. If cm->cm_sgtable is non-NULL it fills the scatter/gather table from segs according to the FIB command type: for RawIo it sets SgCount = nseg and writes address and byte count with Next, Prev and Flags zeroed, for non-64-bit controllers it fills the 32-bit table, otherwise the 64-bit table; in each case it then increases fib->Header.Size by nseg times the entry size (the table must have room for nseg entries, no bound is checked here). It then sets Header.SenderFibAddress = cm_index << 2, ReceiverFibAddress = low 32 bits of cm_fibphys and SenderData = cm_index, performs PREREAD and/or PREWRITE bus_dmamap_sync according to cm_flags, and sets AAC_CMD_MAPPED. With AAC_FLAGS_NEW_COMM it loops calling AAC_SEND_COMMAND until it returns 0, waiting DELAY(5) per attempt; when the retry counter (10,000,000) reaches 0 it unmaps the command, sets AAC_QUEUE_FRZN and requeues the command to the ready queue, but the loop has no exit at that point, so it keeps trying to send (the counter continues to decrease). Otherwise it enqueues the FIB on cm_queue; if aac_enqueue_fib returns EBUSY it unmaps the command, sets AAC_QUEUE_FRZN and requeues it. It returns nothing.
note: Slice cut the head. Not reviewed beyond mechanical rounds; checked against the code. The missing exit in the NEW_COMM retry loop (aac.c:1618-1625) is a real property of the source. Callees (AAC_SEND_COMMAND, aac_enqueue_fib, aac_unmap_command) not read.

name: aac_container_special_command
prose: Static void (aacraid_cam.c:502-837; the packet name aac_cam_action is the caller, the slice is the middle of aac_container_special_command) that answers SCSI commands for a container (logical drive) directly in the driver. It asserts aac_io_lock is held, looks the container up by target id; if it is missing or the LUN is not 0 it sets CAM_DEV_NOT_THERE, calls xpt_done and returns. Then, by SCSI opcode (cmdp): INQUIRY builds standard inquiry data (or the supported-pages and serial number VPD pages; an unsupported page code sets a check-condition error through aac_set_scsi_error, calls xpt_done and returns); REPORT_LUNS, TEST_UNIT_READY, REQUEST_SENSE, READ_CAPACITY, SERVICE_ACTION_IN, MODE_SENSE_6 and SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE fill in the data and set CAM_REQ_CMP (errors for an unsupported service action or mode page set a check condition and return after xpt_done); START_STOP with power management support allocates a command: if allocation fails it freezes the SIM queue, sets CAM_RESRC_UNAVAIL, and queues an AAC_EVENT_CMFREE event (aac_cam_event) and returns without xpt_done (the ccb is completed later by the event), and if the event allocation fails it prints a warning and returns without xpt_done or a queued event; otherwise it builds a container-config FIB (start or stop unit) and waits for it with aacraid_wait_command; and finally CAM_REQ_CMP; unknown opcodes also get CAM_REQ_CMP (the CAM_REQ_INVALID alternative is commented out). Paths that fall out of the switch call xpt_done(ccb) once at the end.
note: Real function is aac_container_special_command; the old drop labelled it as the enclosing dispatcher. Partly read: the byte-level construction of the INQUIRY, READ_CAPACITY, SERVICE_ACTION_IN and MODE_SENSE data (lines 530-640 and 680-810) and the START_STOP completion handling after aacraid_wait_command were only scanned for status settings and returns.

name: acpi_fujitsu_update
prose: Static int (acpi_fujitsu.c:649-758) refreshing the cached Fujitsu hotkey state. It asserts the driver serial lock. If the 'gsif' method exists it computes changed = gsif.value & acpi_fujitsu_method_get(GHKS), else 0. For each of gvol (volume), gmou (pointer), gbls (P8XXX brightness) and gbll (brightness) that exists, it reads the current value with acpi_GetInteger; a failed query prints a message and returns FALSE immediately (the later features are not refreshed and lastValChanged is not updated). Only when the matching changed bit is set does it process the value: volume updates bIsMuted, keeps the setting bits and notifies FN_MUTE or FN_VOLUME with a log line (the volume value is not written back with acpi_fujitsu_method_set); pointer updates bIntPtrEnabled, masks the value, writes it back with acpi_fujitsu_method_set(METHOD_GMOU) and notifies FN_POINTER_ENABLE; P8XXX brightness masks the value, writes it back with method_set(METHOD_GBLS) and notifies FN_LCD_BRIGHTNESS; brightness (gbll) masks the value and notifies FN_LCD_BRIGHTNESS (no write-back). The cached value fields are overwritten by the query for every feature that exists, but the masking and write-back happen only when changed. At the end it stores lastValChanged = changed and returns TRUE.
note: Reviewers: original right (values are masked only when changed); round 15 right (the volume value is not written back through acpi_fujitsu_method_set, 663-686). Callees not read.

name: acpi_hp_sysctl_set
prose: Static int (acpi_hp.c:776-848) applying a sysctl write for the HP laptop driver; it returns 0 on success and -EINVAL when a WMI command fails. It asserts the serial lock. For every method except CMI_DETAIL and VERBOSE it first normalises arg to 0 or 1. Nothing is done (and 0 is returned) when arg equals oldarg. Otherwise by method: WLAN_ENABLED, BLUETOOTH_ENABLED and WWAN_ENABLED send a WMI wireless command (acpi_hp_exec_wmi_command with the enable/disable code for that radio), and return -EINVAL if the command returns non-zero (so these three *_ENABLED methods are written to the hardware, not read-only); ALS sends the ambient-light-sensor WMI command (-EINVAL on failure); the *_ENABLE_IF_RADIO_ON and *_DISABLE_IF_RADIO_OFF methods store the flag in the softc and call acpi_hp_evaluate_auto_on_off; CMI_DETAIL stores the value and resets cmi_order_size to -1 if the SHOW_MAX_INSTANCE bit changed; VERBOSE stores the value. A method code not listed does nothing. Because there is no default case, a read-only or unknown method with arg != oldarg stores nothing, issues no WMI command, and still returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original right (for a method not handled in the switch the call returns 0 without effect); round 15 right (the *_ENABLED methods issue WMI set commands, 785-805).

name: EcSpaceHandler
prose: ACPI operation-region handler for the Embedded Controller (acpi_ec.c:772-843, returns ACPI_STATUS). It returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER if Function is neither ACPI_READ nor ACPI_WRITE, or if Width is not a multiple of 8, Value is NULL or Context is NULL; it returns AE_BAD_ADDRESS if Address + Width / 8 exceeds 256. A Width of 0 passes these checks (the do/while loop then still performs one single-byte transfer). When cold, rebooting or suspending it may run the EC query handler directly if the SCI bit is set and no query is pending. It then takes the EC lock (EcLock; a failure is returned), tries to enable burst mode (a failure is ignored; the burst flag is set only if the data register returns the burst ack), sets *Value = 0 for reads, and transfers byte by byte over Width / 8 addresses (at least one byte): EcRead into the value buffer or EcWrite from it, stopping at the first failing status. It then disables burst mode if it was active, unlocks and returns the status of the last transfer (the failing one, or the last success).
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (Width = 0 passes the checks and transfers one byte, do-while at 806-818); other rounds mechanical. Callees not read.

name: acpi_pwr_switch_consumer
prose: Switches a power consumer to ACPI D-state `state` (acpi_powerres.c:295-513, returns ACPI_STATUS). It returns AE_NOT_FOUND for a NULL consumer. With the powerres serial lock held it finds or registers the consumer (a registration failure goes to out with that status; a missing consumer after registering panics). If the consumer is already in `state` it returns AE_OK. It returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER (via out) when the current state is D3hot and the request is neither D0 nor D3cold, when the current state is D3cold and the request is neither D0 nor D3hot, and for a state value that is not D0..D3cold. Method and resource list names are _PS0/_PR0 ... _PS3/_PR3 (D3cold uses _PS3 and no resource list). If neither the method nor the resource list exists: for D0 it records D0 and returns AE_OK; a D3cold request is converted to D3hot; any state other than D3hot then goes to out with the status left at AE_BAD_PARAMETER; for D3hot it needs _PR0: without _PR0 it returns AE_NOT_FOUND, if _PR0 cannot be evaluated it returns that error, and a _PR0 that is not a valid package gives AE_TYPE; a valid _PR0 is evaluated only to validate it and freed. If a resource list exists it is evaluated (an evaluation error or a non-package type, AE_TYPE, returns). It then dereferences the old resources, references the new list, and calls acpi_pwr_switch_power (a failure is returned). If a _PSx method exists it is evaluated; on failure the recorded state becomes ACPI_STATE_UNKNOWN and the error is returned. On success it records the state, which for a requested D3cold with no _PS3 and no _PR3 is D3hot (converted at 393-394), not the requested state, and returns AE_OK. The lock is released and the evaluated buffer freed on all paths after the lock was taken.
